notes: Session 2. Closed B5-0626, the two-part unattended-run gap the human approved plus commit and push. Origin: the human asked how to tell an agent to execute AGENT_LOOP.md, and the honest answer was that you cannot unless you say so, because the measurement showed a repo-wide search for AGENT_LOOP returning seven references of which EVERY one was a document written ABOUT the file and ZERO from any executable. Seven citations and zero invocations: the file was extremely well referenced and completely inert, which is the same number you get from a rule quoted constantly and obeyed never. Meanwhile run-queue.ps1, the one automated path that exists and which has the right shape of one task per fresh process, told every agent it invoked at line 218 to read .agent/HANDOFF.md, which is misleading in a way that produces a specific wrong action rather than merely old text: its section 7 states b5ccg/src is RED at -source 6 when it has been green since 2026-09-21, and its section 9 tells the reader to claim B5-0001, DONE since 2026-09-21. An unattended agent obeying that literally would have created a claim on a closed task, which is exactly the orphan class B5-0622 spent a task closing the protocol against, so the automation was one step from undoing the best work of the session by following a document nobody had re-read since day one. PART 1 repointed the task template at AGENT_LOOP.md while keeping 00_BOOT.md as the boot step, and rewriting it surfaced four rules the template was missing that only the new procedure carries, folded in rather than left as tidying: the sanitised agent-id in the report filename, the reusable-lesson line as a NEW file under PATTERNS with supersede-never-rewrite, the binding heartbeat schema, and the re-read-the-row-still-OPEN check. The template also carried its own stale pointer, mark BLOCKED per step 7 when verify is step 8, the SECOND instance of that exact defect in two tasks after B5-0625 found the same class in the human-supplied prompt at step 10 when it was really 11. Added one line telling agents NOT to read HANDOFF.md, since an agent that remembers the old pointer will look for it. PART 2 marked HANDOFF.md superseded in its own frontmatter with a machine-readable superseded_by block, set status to Superseded and explicitly not authority, and put a banner above the body that NAMES BOTH false statements specifically rather than saying only that the document is old, on the reasoning that a reader who knows which two claims are false can act while one told merely that a document is stale will skim and follow section 9 anyway. Sections 1 through 6 left intact and marked broadly accurate; the file was not deleted. Verified by RUNNING the tool rather than reading the diff: -DryRun exits 0, no crash, no duplicate warning, same head task, template no longer contains Read .agent/HANDOFF.md and now contains Do NOT read it, and all four TASK_ID placeholders are substituted by an all-occurrences String.Replace. Caveat disclosed not papered: ConvertFrom-Yaml does not exist in Windows PowerShell 5.1, so the frontmatter was NOT machine-parsed and was verified structurally by delimiter position and interior line classification instead, which is a weaker guarantee and is recorded as such. Gates green: compile.bat Build successful, runner exit 0, heartbeats 27/27 conforming, ledger 324 rows no duplicate ids. Left untouched: Buffy (glm-5.3-flash)'s live B5-0620 claim scoped to HeadlessConformanceTest.java, their untracked B5-0612 report, and the SCOPE_RELEASES logs. Reusable lesson: a procedure nothing launches is documentation, not instruction, and the automated path is the one path nobody re-reads because it is the one path nobody watches.
